extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Popular Science Monthly: educated general public, scientists, amateur naturalists, and practitioners interested in scientific books and reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative criteria for reviewing and assessing scientific and popular-science books, essays, and manuals — covering accuracy, evidence, style, illustrations, intended audience, and utility for practitioners or students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithful and complete reporting/translation
rubrics_metrics.description: We have not printed an imperfect report of Virchow's address, but a full and faithful translation of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy and completeness in reproducing speeches or primary texts are essential; reviewers/publishers should avoid truncated or distorted reports and aim for faithful translation and full reporting so readers can judge the original argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture the full breadth of a controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring out the 'breadth of the collision between Virchow and Haeckel.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To convey a dispute properly, present both sides (e.g., printing both speeches side by side) and provide sufficient context so readers can appreciate scope, depth, and momentum of the disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical rigor and careful handling of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A question of the nature, extent, and validity of evidence ... taken up as a logician, in a very quiet way, with much delicate humor and a peculiar charm of style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess claims by examining the nature, extent, and validity of supporting evidence; clear logical argumentation (even when calmly presented) that points out baseless conclusions is valued in scientific writing and reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid enforcing a foregone conclusion; be unbiased
rubrics_metrics.description: His object is to enforce a foregone conclusion rather than to conduct a critical and unbiased inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not begin by asserting the conclusion they wish to reach; sound scholarship requires open, candid, and critical inquiry that engages evidence before drawing conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage directly and tenaciously with important opposing evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: We fail to see him grapple so directly or tenaciously as we could have wished with the evidences of man's existence during ... the last glacial epoch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When controversial points exist, a credible work must confront the strongest counter-evidence and important issues (e.g., implements in till or gravels), rather than setting them aside summarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis: consolidate scattered evidence into a coherent focus
rubrics_metrics.description: To bring to a focus the scattered rays of light which the most recent inquiries have shed upon the chronology of human life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuable contributions gather, correlate, and synthesize dispersed facts and recent inquiries to present a clearer overall picture and to check speculative overreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and avoidance of mere compilation
rubrics_metrics.description: Declining to follow in the beaten paths of compilation, and avoiding a mere restatement of rudiments ... has adopted an intermediate and independent course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should avoid simple compilation or restatement of basics; original perspective, selective emphasis on current problems, and independent treatment increase a work's worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate scope and audience targeting (popular vs specialist)
rubrics_metrics.description: An excellent popular account ... intended not only for professional potters and decorators, but for that large class of persons who are seeking to acquire this art ... The author does not assume for it that it is in any sense a substitute for a text-book ... intended to be used in connection with anatomical demonstrations, charts, diagrams, and the microscope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match technical detail, terminology, and scope to intended readers: omit excessive technical terms for popular or introductory audiences; explicitly state whether a work is a popular account, a professional manual, or a supplement to formal instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and pedagogical usefulness of illustrations and plates
rubrics_metrics.description: His book is elaborately illustrated ... the colored map of radiation and absorption spectra ... photographic plates showing actual effects more accurately than would be possible with engravings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of good illustrations, colored maps, and photographic plates can materially enhance understanding (especially for amateurs and experimenters); such features should be accurate and appropriate to the topics being taught or demonstrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost–benefit justification for expensive features
rubrics_metrics.description: This feature somewhat enhances the cost of the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors/authors should weigh the instructional value of costly inclusions (plates, color maps) against increased price; justify added expense by clear pedagogical or evidentiary benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value added in new editions and correction of errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefixed to the volume an elaborate essay of very great interest ... in revision the author has confined himself to the correction of typographical errors in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New editions should provide meaningful new material, corrections, or elaborations that justify purchase; mere reprints with only minor fixes are less valuable unless prefatory material substantially enhances understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, elegance of style, and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: This elegant volume ... with much delicate humor and a peculiar charm of style ... an admirable statement ... an instructive volume of moderate size on questions at present most interesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear, elegant exposition and an appropriate tone (including measured humor when fitting) improve readability and persuasiveness; good style is an important criterion in evaluating popular and scholarly works alike.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical instruction and applicability for practitioners and amateurs
rubrics_metrics.description: To describe the laws which govern the form and decoration of pottery; and to give practical instruction in the art of painting ... intended not only for the benefit of professional potters and decorators, but for that large class ... seeking to acquire this art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuals should include actionable, practical guidance (techniques, laws of form/decoration) targeted to both professionals and serious amateurs when that is the stated aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: State the role of the work relative to formal education (aid vs substitute)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepared merely as an aid to students ... does not assume ... that it is in any sense a substitute for a text-book, or other book of reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should clearly declare whether a work is a primary textbook, a brief syllabus/aid, or a supplement to demonstrations and laboratory work so instructors and students can use it appropriately.
